title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching, quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token inference cost and make cost/latency tradeoffs easier to consume across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) new autotune defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching that are conservative but effective for common production workloads, 2) model-level quantization profiles (recommended quantize/precision settings) surfaced to the runtime and model catalog, and 3) a lightweight unit-economics (uecon) tooling surface in the Console and CLI to estimate per-route token cost and recommended config changes. Implementation summary: - Add a new autotune/config schema and default profiles (pkg/autotune/config.go, pkg/autotune/profiles.go). Defaults selected from recent perf runs (see ENG-4572) and are safe for latency-sensitive routes: smaller max_batch_size for <200ms target, aggressive KV cache prefixes for repeated prefixes. - Plug autotune into the router so new requests can be annotated with recommended batching/cache overrides at route-level (pkg/router/autotune_integration.go). - Add model metadata for quantization profiles and a migration path for existing models to include a recommended profile (redwood-model-registry/metadata/quant_profiles.go, cmd/modelctl migrate-quant). - Expose a Unit Economics tool in Console (cmd/console/static/uecon.html + api handlers) and CLI (cmd/cli uecon estimate --route) that uses historical token distributions + current profiles to produce per-request and monthly cost estimates. - Tests: unit + integration tests covering autotune heuristics, quant profile parsing, and uecon-estimator (tests/autotune_integration_test.go, tests/uecon_cli_test.go). Checklist: - [x] Add autotune defaults and schema - [x] Integrate autotune with routing and config propagation - [x] Add quantization profile support in model registry - [x] Add uecon estimator (CLI + Console UI) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs and migration guide (docs/cost-optimization.md) Backwards compatibility: The autotune defaults are opt-in via a new cluster-level flag (autotune.enabled=false by default). Existing deployments will not change behavior until the flag is set. The quantization profiles are additive metadata and do not affect runtime unless a model is explicitly configured to use a profile. Rollout plan: land behind feature flag, enable on canary clusters for 2 weeks while monitoring cost & latency dashboards. Related: ENG-4572 (autotune tuning), ENG-4620 (uecon estimator), SUP-234 (customer request to reduce token costs).

notes_for_release: Added opt-in autotune defaults for batching/caching, model quantization profile support, and a basic unit-economics estimator in Console/CLI. Operators can enable autotune via the cluster flag autotune.enabled=true. No runtime behavior changes unless enabled. See docs/cost-optimization.md for rollout guidance and migration steps.
release_notes:
- Opt-in autotune defaults (batching + KV cache) to reduce per-token cost
- Model quantization profiles in model registry (opt-in)
- Unit economics estimator in Console + CLI (estimates per-route cost and suggested config)
additional_context: This PR is the first coordinated step to expose actionable cost controls to engineers and product owners. Follow-ups planned: - autotune learning loop (collect feedback and automatically tune per-route) - expanded quant profiles for more models and hardware targets - integration with Dedicated capacity autoscaler for cost-aware routing.
